vanilla.note: Recorded from docs/perf/v1.6-check.json, which ran the DEFAULT `--perf-test` configuration (Barebones style, Shaders Medium: it has bloom/shafts/water GPU times) under the script's default row name 'vanilla'; M4 runs of this row must use the same configuration until a real Vanilla row is recorded here. Its three flights differ: 97.5 FPS (not vsync-limited), then 60.0 and 60.0 (vsync on a 60 Hz display), so the median average_fps (60.00) is the display's cap. Single launch: the ratios below are the M1 baseline's (docs/perf/baseline.json), to be replaced by measured noise once the M4 has three launches of --runs 3.

average_fps.reason: M1 baseline's ratio (measured noise there: medians spread 10.5%, widened to twice that); the M4 has one launch so far.

one_percent_low_fps.reason: M1 baseline's ratio (measured noise there: spread 27.0%, widened to twice that); the M4 has one launch so far.

accepted.reason: Kenzo asked for an M4 baseline from docs/perf/v1.6-check.json (chat, 2026-11-15)

barebones-native.note: M68: Barebones + Shaders Medium, full screen at the display's native size, vsync on, Auto Render Scale (75% at 2940x1846). Reference is Kenzo's MacBook Air M4 (Mac16,12, 60 Hz, no ProMotion), docs/perf/m4-native-vsync-on.txt: 3594 frames in 60 s, 1% low 51, worst 49.7 ms. Budgets: 95% of the 60 Hz refresh and of the measured 1% low; missed_frame_pct max 1 is M68's own target (under 1% missed frames); that file doesn't print it, so the first M4 run with this build is the first check. The Mac mini that builds the game can't measure this row and is refused; run it on the M4.
